turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I still haven't got anything for my dad and the holidays are in two weeks.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Still time. Does he like gadgets, or would something like a nice sweater or a cooking class feel more like him?

contexts.pending: a gadget, clothing, or an experience for dad

Have you thought about it? What kind of gift feels most like your dad?
welcome_back: Welcome back. We were brainstorming a holiday gift for your dad.
Hi again. Any closer to knowing what your dad would like, a gadget or something else?

endings.user: A cooking class. He's been making the same three dishes for years.
endings.moshi: Ha, perfect. Pick one with a cuisine he's never tried.

endings.user: Probably a gadget, he loves anything with buttons.
endings.moshi: Easy then. A wireless meat thermometer is a fun one for a dad who grills.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Our office is doing a gift exchange with a twenty dollar limit.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Fun. Do you want to play it safe with something everyone would like, like good chocolate, or go for a funny gag gift?

contexts.pending: safe gift or funny gag gift for the office exchange

Alright, did you decide? Chocolate or a gag gift?
welcome_back: Welcome back. You were choosing between a safe gift and a gag gift for work.
There you are. Still thinking about the office exchange, safe or silly?

endings.user: Safe. I don't know half those people well enough for jokes.
endings.moshi: Smart. A box of nice chocolates or a fancy hot cocoa set works for almost anyone.

endings.user: Funny, our team loves that stuff.
endings.moshi: Then go for it. A desk sized punching bag usually gets a good laugh.

turns.text: I want to get my best friend something special this year.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Sweet. Would you rather make something by hand, like a photo book of your trips, or buy something she's been wanting?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Oh, both sound good.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Take a moment. Homemade or store bought?

contexts.pending: homemade photo book or something she wants

endings.user: The photo book. We've done so many trips together.
endings.moshi: She'll love it. Start this week, since printing can take a while.

endings.user: I'll buy her the headphones she keeps talking about.
endings.moshi: Great choice. Tuck a handwritten note in the box to make it personal.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: {friend}, what did you get your brother last year?

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: What's a good gift for someone who says they don't want anything?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Something consumable works well, like nice coffee, a good candle or a fancy jam. It won't add clutter.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: She doesn't drink coffee. She's really into / I guess gardening, mostly.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then try a set of good seeds or a pair of quality garden gloves. Gardeners always wear gloves out.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Gloves feel a bit boring though.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Fair. A small herb planter for her kitchen window is more fun and still useful.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Ooh, I like that. Can I make one myself?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Definitely. Get a wooden box, some potting soil and three herbs like basil, thyme and mint.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How much should I spend on gifts for my coworkers?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Most people keep it small, around ten to fifteen dollars each. Nobody expects much at work.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Do I need to get one for my boss too?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: It's usually not expected. If you want to, a card or a group gift from the team is safest.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: I was going to bake cookies for everyone / is that too cheap?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Not at all, homemade cookies are often the favorite. Put them in little tins and they look really thoughtful.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: How many should I put in each one?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Six to eight is plenty. Maybe mix two kinds so it feels like a treat.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: My nephew is turning into a teenager and I have no clue what he likes anymore.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: That's a tough age to shop for. Gift cards are popular with teens because they get to choose.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Isn't a gift card kind of lazy, though?

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Some people think so, but teens usually love them. Pair it with something small and fun so it feels personal.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Like what? He's into skateboarding, / I think.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Then a card for a skate shop plus a set of cool stickers for his board would be great.

turns.speaker: user
turns.text: Actually, maybe I'll just ask his mom first.

turns.speaker: moshi
turns.text: Good idea. She'll know if he already has something or has been hinting about anything.

option_sets.lead_in: I need help choosing a holiday gift for my wife.
options: The first idea is a weekend at a little cabin in the mountains, just the two of us.
Then there's a really nice leather bag she looked at twice but didn't buy.
And the last option is a pottery class for both of us, every Thursday for a month.
moshi_comment: The cabin weekend and the pottery class are both about spending time together, which often means more than an object. The bag is a safe bet since she clearly wanted it. If she's been busy and tired lately, the cabin might be the best gift of all.
All three are lovely. Does she prefer relaxing or trying new things? If she likes new things, the pottery class gives you a month of date nights, otherwise I'd go with the cabin.

option_sets.lead_in: I can't decide what to get my roommate for the holidays.
options: One option is a fancy pour over coffee set, since she drinks coffee all day.
Another is a big soft blanket for the couch, because she's always cold.
Or I could get her tickets to the comedy show she mentioned last week.
The last idea is a plant for her room, maybe one that's really hard to kill.
moshi_comment: The comedy tickets show you actually listened, which is always a nice feeling. The coffee set is practical and she'd use it every day. The blanket and the plant are sweet but a bit more generic.
I'd go for the comedy show, especially if you could go together. If money's tight, the blanket is cheap and she'd use it all winter.
